title: OST crackles under heavy loading
status: Still present in v0.0.30-rc1 (maintainer, WinUAE, 7 October 2026): heavy music crackling going from the ship's hull to the deck, and small crackles entering the Census and Excise Office. Control cases from the same playtest, both without disk loads: no crackle while choosing character attributes or reading the release papers in the Census office. Points at the mixer starving during blocking loads rather than at the music path. Project priority: the soundtrack must stay clean through loads. Related WIN-05 history retained; cause and independent reproduction pending. The maintainer, 24 October 2026: the crackle depends on the emulator: FS-UAE barely crackles during the loads, WinUAE much more. Fits the mixer starving during a blocking load: the length of the load (the emulated disk timing) and the emulator s sound buffer decide how much of the gap is heard; real hardware is likely closer to WinUAE. Source (triage of 24 October 2026): no music or mixer update between the map and model reads (common.c, model.c, sv_main.c), unlike aw_head.c. Repair (v0.0.51, fixable now): service the music between chunks of those reads; verify on WinUAE through the opening (hull to deck, the census office).
where: Music mixer during heavy loads (ship hull to deck, entering Census office)
severity_reason: The music never crackling through loads is the project s golden standard (the maintainer, 24 October 2026); the opening is the first thing every player hears

status: Open: the engine default is chim_zone_kib 6,864 with a 2 x 384 KiB frame-world pool (0d8bf4f, shipped in v0.0.33): 6,242,304 bytes of chunk room, which the heap gate reads from the engine source (engine_limits.chim_memory); the interim 7,680 KiB builder budget is gone. Open: a zone each world states itself (proposed). PERSISTING in v0.0.49 and v0.0.50 (24 October 2026): the boot smokes log CHIM chunk zone-full retries in Balmora (the zone locked 7,021,952 of 7,028,736 bytes; chunks 394, 401, 360 and others retried): v0.0.49 final at 32 MB 234 lines, v0.0.50 final 306 at 32 MB and 511 at 16 MB. Every smoke passed (the chunks load on a retry). On the v0.0.51 list (persisting bugs, item 0.4). The zone does not grow with Fast RAM: chim_zone_kib stays 6,864 KiB (engine/aga/src/chim/chim_world.c) at 32 MB as at 16 MB, so the retries happen at both (the maintainer asked, 24 October 2026); the RAM past 16 MB goes to the CHIM cache bank, not the zone. Repair (v0.0.51): size the zone from the Fast RAM found at start, like the heap and the cache bank, and gate the build on Balmora loading with no zone-full retry at 32 MB. Where it bites: the old town frames. Seyda Neen, Balmora and Vivec were built as one big frame each, before the one-cell region frames, so a whole town s chunks share the one fixed zone (the maintainer, 24 October 2026: the original cities might have this same fixed setting problem). The retries in the v0.0.49 and v0.0.50 smokes are all in Balmora. To check for all three in v0.0.51 at 16 and 32 MB; the old town frames as ordinary region frames (v0.0.51 list) would end it for good.

title: Roads and paths on the ground look blocky: each texture square is drawn with hard edges instead of blending into its neighbours
status: Reported 18 October 2026 by the maintainer ('the road paths look like shit atm'; every path of the game): a path breaks into separate squares instead of reading as one track. Morrowind's land texture layer is 16 x 16 squares per cell and blends neighbouring squares; ours draws one texture per square with hard edges. Planned A/B, first option the maintainer's (20:04): (d) DIAGONAL SPLITS: where a square's texture meets a different texture on two adjacent sides (a corner of a stair-step edge), split that square along its diagonal into two triangles, each with one texture, so stair-steps become 45-degree edges (marching-squares over the texture grid; about one extra face per split square, no new textures). Then, if needed: (a) baked transition textures for the edge pairs that occur, (b) a dithered edge band baked into the surfaces, (c) finer squares along roads. Measured in faces, memory and frame time; OpenMW at the same pose.

title: 16 MB of Fast RAM no longer holds the whole game: 32 MB is the safe minimum, 16 MB starts with a warning
status: Fixed in v0.0.48-dev2 (branch v0.0.48-fast-ram-32), decided for the project 23 October 2026: for now the game requires 32 MB of Fast RAM, the safe minimum, which should be enough for the entire game; more RAM is used automatically (heap 13 MiB at 32 MB, 20 at 64, 24 at 128, unchanged). Below 32 MB the boot check shows the Fast RAM row as [!] WARN and, under the checklist's closing line, the note 'NOTE: AmiWind has grown since v0.0.48: 32 MB of Fast RAM is now the minimum. Only N MB Fast RAM found, hence the game will start but may load more often. Press ENTER to continue anyway.' with a ten-second countdown under it (ENTER skips; it never blocks, so unattended 16 MB runs go on); the engine repeats the note without a wait on the CLI, the console and the startup logo. The launcher, the playtest packages' emulator configs and the shipped play presets start with 32 MB; 16 MB stays a choice with a warning. Found 22-23 October 2026 with every outdoor NPC and creature placed (781 actors in 336 CHIM region frames): 14 frames need more model cache than the 16 MB baseline gives (about 2.1 MB; worst rcp2_m7 over by 2.0 MB); actor models per frame 624 KB median, 4.13 MB max; with a 24 MiB heap (about 15.7 MB of cache) every frame fits; interiors: largest Balmora room set 4.10 MB of a 7.03 MB room zone; on 16 MB the engine evicts and reloads models: slower, not a crash.
where: Fast RAM requirement: boot check, engine start, launcher and emulator presets
severity_reason: on 16 MB 14 outdoor frames overflow the model cache: models are evicted and loaded again, slower, not a crash

title: The CHIM and room stages ran side by side at 42 of 44 GiB and were both throttled to one worker for over ten minutes
status: Fixed for v0.0.48 on the branch v0.0.48-fix-build-speed. Cause confirmed: a pool's idle worker processes keep the memory they reached, so the scheduler's cut stopped new units but freed nothing and the memory never came back under the line. Each worker pool under the scheduler now ends its idle workers above the stage's allowance after about 20 s (build_parallel._watch_idle_workers; ordered maps of a stage pool through tools/pool_status.py); new ones start when the allowance grows. Measured: 8 idle workers 1,057 MiB -> 1 worker 132 MiB after a cut to 1 (tests/test_pool_idle_retire.py); room batches stage cut to 2 of 16 at 60 s: 14 idle workers ended, process memory 1.95 GiB -> 0.57 GiB during the cut, outputs byte-identical. Scheduling only: no stage key changes (checked over every tools script, base 178df662). Peaks apart: not scheduled apart; chim-room-batches is off the critical path, and with the workers ending a cut above the critical line frees memory, so the guard gives the share back instead of holding both stages at one worker.

title: The alias model budget is still the 16 MB era's 512 KiB: two NPCs fall back to standing-only animations
status: Fixed in v0.0.48 (branch v0.0.48-fix-content-32mb, 23 October 2026): the actors byte budget is sized for 32 MB of Fast RAM, 768 KiB (npc_anim.ACTOR_BYTE_BUDGET: room and town residents, the actor library), the engine direct alias stream limit (model.c AW_ALIAS_STREAM_LIMIT, the heap estimate alias_stream_heap.STREAM_LIMIT). The stream decodes a model straight into its Cache block, with no staging and no Hunk, so a model over the 512 KiB staging limit loads the same way on 16 MB, where the Cache evicts older models for it (native test: a 536 KB model streams with malloc failing, to the bytes the older Hunk path decodes). The malloc staging (AW_ALIAS_STAGING_LIMIT) and the player models keep 512 KiB. Measured on all 1,769 room residents and 415 actor library appearances (read only): under 512 KiB, 161 kits were over it at their first vertex rung and were baked at a lower one, and Neloth and Ienas Nadus fell back to their standing model; with 768 KiB none is reduced and none falls back (every kit fits: at most 666 faces x 64 samples, 720,032 bytes). Neloth and Ienas Nadus get the full react+full kit (movers 682,312 and 681,492 bytes, standing models 331,316 and 331,060). Cost: those standing models +12.6 KB on average (largest +89.6 KB, 2.2 MB in all), movers +3.8 MB in all; two movers at once are at most 1.44 MB of the Cache, within the 2 MiB Hunk gap of the 16 MB baseline, so no room or frame is marked for it. Not yet in a build or in game.
where: engine/aga/src/model.c AW_ALIAS_STREAM_LIMIT; tools/npc_anim.py ACTOR_BYTE_BUDGET
